title: Host the upstream worker with acknowledged startup and drain
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Runledger already owns claims, leases and durable retries. The process host must preserve that ownership while observing worker startup, failure and shutdown.

## Scope and ownership

Use the exact startup witness from docs/reference-compatibility.md, not supervisor build completion as readiness. Lifecycle tests use the isolated fixtures and driven cleanup from batter-kjl. Signal upstream shutdown during process drain and await its owned shutdown/join result with the full documented budget, including abort cleanup. This task owns hosting; provider certainty/reconciliation belongs to batter-8q8.2. Do not supervise or respawn each upstream internal loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Startup/schema/registry/witness failure prevents readiness and follows partial-startup cleanup. A controlled initialization witness succeeds through the actual registered handler; acknowledgements state what that witness proves, without claiming every hidden loop initialized.
- Exercise normal drain and returned worker failure using the real upstream runtime and live fixture. Preserve the error returned by upstream; where upstream returns only its first failure and logs later failures, document that visibility limit rather than promise Batter collected hidden errors.
- Request stop-claiming at drain before forced cancellation. An already in-flight upstream claim may finish after the stop request; tests observe/classify it and do not promise a linearized upstream no-claim barrier absent a verified API.
- Outer grace includes the selected shutdown API's abort-cleanup allowance. Dropping its supervisor requests shutdown/detaches in the inspected candidate and is not proof of join. Timeout/panic/forced stop retains uncertain transitive termination and conservative dependency cleanup.
- Each job attempt gets fresh OperationContext budget and trusted dependencies independent of the submitting request token/deadline. Business denial and durable retry/reconcile outcomes remain successful task values rather than fatal process Err.
- Record upstream attempts and handler invocations independently; local replay does not multiply durable attempts. Provider-effect identity/restart proof remains batter-8q8.2.

title: Add per-attempt deadlines capped by remaining total budget
description:
## Outcome and rationale

A single slow attempt should be bounded without granting the next attempt a fresh total deadline.

## Scope

Add a source-compatible opt-in per-attempt maximum duration. Preserve existing `execute`/`execute_with_jitter` signatures, default behavior, and the meaning of their currently exhaustively matchable public error enums. Use a new opt-in entrypoint/result boundary for the additional typed attempt-timeout outcome instead of relabeling it as expiration of the original total context. Validate a positive representable attempt duration before any factory work. Immediately before each attempt, after its preceding backoff, derive `attempt_deadline = min(original_context.deadline(), attempt_start + attempt_maximum)` with checked arithmetic and downward cancellation. The input context may already be a shortened work phase; never recover its reserved finalization time or refresh the original total deadline. Reaching an attempt deadline is terminal for this execution, just like cancellation: it does not authorize another attempt or invoke expected-error classification. Preserve the latest earlier application error and the count of factories actually invoked. Keep panic propagation and destruction/cancellation behavior of OperationContext::run. Add a runnable example using distinct total and attempt limits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Paused-time tests prove the deadline formula for the first and subsequent attempts, including a parent deadline shorter than the requested attempt limit, backoff consuming original total time, and use of a shortened `OperationPhases::work()` context. A later attempt may start with less than its requested maximum remaining; the maximum is a cap, not a minimum useful-work reservation.
- The opt-in result distinguishes an attempt cap expiring while total time remains from the original total deadline expiring. At a tied attempt/total deadline report total deadline; cancellation wins over either deadline, and an expired deadline wins over simultaneously ready work completion, preserving existing boundary precedence.
- Attempt timeout stops the sequence with no classifier call for the interrupted attempt and no next factory. Count only invoked factories: initial interruption reports zero, first-attempt timeout reports one with no prior error, and a later-attempt timeout retains the previous concrete error and actual started count.
- Cancellation during backoff or before the next factory retains the prior error/count without incrementing either attempt or future optional retry-token debit. A started attempt's child scope is cancelled and its owned future destroyed on completion/interruption; parent cancellation remains downward and no arbitrary spawned task is claimed joined.
- Zero/unrepresentable attempt configuration is rejected without starting a factory. No opt-in path catches panics as retryable errors. Existing public entrypoint behavior and exhaustive consumer matches keep compiling, and new public APIs have rustdoc plus an example.

title: Exercise cancellation and admission races under sustained scheduling
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Strengthen executable evidence for Batter's small native Rust/Tokio operational contracts: who owns work, what bounds it, who observes failures and when dependencies may close. This makes the foundation easier for AI coding agents to use and modify without guessing hidden framework behavior.

The existing tests cover specific failure paths and two 64-iteration multi-thread races. They do not implement seeded schedule exploration or sustained contention. In the 2026-09-08 audit of commit 5db16f6f18fd918d3d3558a68843120bf9a13b79, all 60 focused admission/lifecycle/operation/process-ownership tests passed a disposable variant that gave descendants independent semaphore capacity. A deterministic capacity-one ancestor/descendant probe passed on the original implementation and rejected that variant. This is a confirmed coverage gap, not a demonstrated production defect. Existing race-loop iteration bounds also do not contain a hung readiness/barrier/result wait.

## Scope

Add test-local seeded scenario generation, controlled scheduling checkpoints and sustained bounded multi-thread stress around completion, readiness, root/descendant admission, drain, forced cancellation and receipt/driver drop. Keep the current deterministic failure-contract tests and add regressions for discovered defects. Implementation fixes must remain scoped to demonstrated contract violations. Do not add a production scheduler, Effect runtime, DI abstraction, resource framework or new public API merely to support the harness.

The scenario families are admission/capacity, operation cancellation/completion, readiness/drain, task/report error retention, driver/receipt ownership and escalation/cleanup. Required cases must be selected explicitly rather than left to chance in a random sample. Keep harness implementation with the foundation tests; generic batter-test-support remains a leaf.

## Contract distinctions for the test oracle

- OperationContext children inherit cancellation downward. Finishing an operation cancels its operation scope; it does not join arbitrary spawned tasks.
- ProcessScope grants descendant admission while its ancestor is active. An already admitted descendant has process lifetime; ancestor completion invalidates further submissions through that scope, not the child's ownership. Roots and descendants share one queued-plus-executing capacity bound.
- Process admission is linearized with drain. Bulkhead cancellation preflight is not atomic with concurrent semaphore acquisition; admitted operations still need their own check/run boundary. Do not invent a stronger Bulkhead guarantee in these tests.
- Owned-driver waiter cancellation and last-owner drop differ from dropping caller-owned run_until. The former preserve the independently driven completion protocol on a live runtime; the latter requests emergency cancellation without promising awaited cleanup.
- Readiness observations and admission decisions must be judged using established happens-before order or contract-permitted overlap, not timestamps sampled after the fact. Likewise, eventual task success is not sufficient to label an abort request false.
- Retain only bounded, generic schedule metadata and numeric test IDs. Do not serialize internal reports or print Debug/Display of application errors/panic payloads. Test diagnostic redaction with synthetic returned-error sentinels and scoped capture; use generic panic-fixture payloads and account explicitly for default panic-hook output without installing library globals.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add a discoverable, bounded multi-thread stress profile for 2 and 4 Tokio workers. For each worker count, exercise at least 32 recorded seeds, 64 supervisor lifecycles, and 4,096 successfully completed finite tasks across those lifecycles. Require overlapping roots/descendants, saturation followed by capacity reuse, and coverage of every scenario family below; fail if a required family or workload minimum was not exercised. Counts are exploration minima, not correctness or throughput claims.
2. Prove shared capacity with a deterministic capacity-one case: while an ancestor occupies the only permit, descendant submission returns Full without invoking its factory. Under mixed contention, independently account for queued plus executing roots and descendants, demonstrate the configured bound, and check rejected factories remain inert. Receipt drop/cancel must neither release capacity early nor cancel admitted work; real completion must permit reuse.
3. Exercise root admission versus drain, active descendant admission during drain, descendant admission versus forced cancellation/task failure, and escaped-scope admission versus ancestor completion. Controlled orderings must check both allowed and forbidden cases; genuinely overlapping calls may take either contract-permitted ordering. A completed drain request forbids later roots; observed force/failure or an expired scope forbids later descendants.

Preserve the distinct process-descendant lifetime and Bulkhead preflight contracts stated below.
5. Exercise application readiness approval, every component startup acknowledgement, critical exit and drain in competing orders. Ready requires the driver plus approval plus all acknowledgements. Check ordered observations never return to Ready after Draining/Stopped, including acknowledgements/approval attempted after drain has completed.
6. Maintain a bounded test-owned ledger of submissions and expected outcomes, independent of ShutdownReport counters. Reconcile admitted successes, task errors, panics, aborts and unjoined work with receipts and the complete report; preserve all expected task and cleanup error identities/categories without formatting their contents. Mix concurrent failures and dropped receipts. Exercise shutdown-waiter cancellation during cleanup, last-owner drop with retained observers, and caller-owned driver drop before/after first poll under their different contracts.

A deliberately stuck fixture must fail visibly, terminate/reap within the watchdog protocol and retain bounded diagnostics even if Tokio cannot run timers. A seed reproduces scenario generation, not the Tokio scheduler. Demonstrate repeatable rejection of an injected fault from a recorded controlled schedule; preserve uncontrolled stress traces as diagnostics and reduce any discovered race defect to a deterministic regression before claiming it is reproducible or fixed.

title: Separate HTTP observation from request admission and deadlines
description:
## Problem and reproduced evidence

HTTP observation currently shares the request admission/deadline boundary. In crates/batter-axum/src/lib.rs, request_scope_inner constructs the private HttpObservation before the readiness gate. Consequently, gate rejections are already observed, but probes and fallback mounted outside request_scope are not. A downstream consumer removed its outer TraceLayer during adoption and lost those HTTP completion events. The Batter HTTP example also merges probes after applying request_scope, so the coverage problem is reproducible from the recommended composition.

Investigation on 2026-09-08 executed against an actual downstream router using pinned Batter revision e5f2f04b2dbb349d08085caf177f662fcbc89812 and Axum 0.8.9. Its adapter implementation matches the local checkout apart from a platform documentation line. With an INFO tracing capture:

| Scenario | Response status | HTTP completion events |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Application success | 200 | 1 |
| Liveness probe | 200 | 0 |
| Readiness failure | 503 | 0 |
| Unmatched fallback | 404 | 0 |
| Method rejection on an application route | 405 | 1 |
| Drain rejection | 503 | 1 |

On Rust 1.98.1, all 16 Batter adapter tests and all six downstream HTTP tests passed. Their passing results do not establish coverage of this composition: tests/telemetry.rs exercises fallback by installing the combined request_scope across its router. Existing tests/scoped_dispatch.rs proves aborted combined middleware retains the original subscriber and nested span destruction, but does not exercise independent observation.

The disposable reproduction remains at /tmp/batter-http-investigation-zpp1c_u_/src/main.rs on the investigating machine. This is transient supporting evidence, not a required future test fixture; the matrix and assembly instructions here suffice to recreate it using generic routes.

## Delivery scope

Add independent HTTP observation middleware to batter-axum, with no lifecycle handle or deadline policy requirement. Keep HttpObservation private. Add an admission/deadline entry point that retains RequestPolicy, readiness admission, native OperationContext insertion, forced cancellation, and configured failure rendering. Preserve request_scope as a compatibility wrapper over the shared observation and admission implementations. RequestPolicy continues to combine readiness and deadlines; this task separates observation from that combined policy.

Update the HTTP example and adoption guidance to assemble guarded application routes using the admission-only entry point, merge unguarded probes and fallback, apply observation to the assembled router, and apply trusted server request identity outermost. The outer observer must surround middleware that rejects or transforms responses within the intended observed boundary. Migration must replace the inner combined request_scope when adding outer observation, so the supported composition emits one HTTP completion per request. Explicitly document the behavior of nesting the observer with the legacy combined wrapper; do not accidentally promise deduplication.

Preserve first-poll dispatcher capture using batter::telemetry::with_current_dispatch. Observation guards, instrumented futures and their nested spans must all remain inside its protected future through polling and full destruction. Preserve method normalization, matched route templates or <unmatched>, actual response status, outcome and latency, without logging raw paths, query values, headers, bodies, error contents or untrusted methods. Trusted request correlation remains application-owned.

## Axum composition constraint

Axum 0.8.9 Router::layer runs after routing and only covers routes/fallback assembled before the layer is applied. A route appended afterward bypasses it. A literal Tower wrapper outside routing sees no MatchedPath when the current observer creates its span, even for a matched route. Both behaviors were executed in the reproduction. Use the assembled-router placement to preserve sanitized route templates; test new routes added through that normal assembly path and state the late-route limitation. Do not describe the conceptual ordering diagram as literal pre-routing middleware unless route metadata capture is redesigned and tested.

Primary reference: https://docs.rs/crate/axum/0.8.9/source/src/docs/routing/layer.md ; also inspect the resolved axum source and record version-specific semantics in docs/references.md at implementation time.

## Ownership and limits

Owning package: batter-axum. Parent: batter-faj, observability across ownership boundaries. This work is independently actionable; it does not wait for database reference work, exporters, request metadata extraction, or the separate upstream admission integration in batter-97p. Related work is context, not a blocking dependency.

The observed lifetime ends at response construction. A dropped, polled response future may emit dropped without a response status; dropping a body after response construction is a different lifetime. Do not imply body streaming, WebSocket ownership, universal disconnect propagation, panic recovery, runtime-death finalization, or exactly-once log delivery. Library global subscribers and panic hooks remain forbidden.

## Required dependent updates and verification

Update public rustdoc and a compiling example, crates/batter-axum/README.md and relevant package guidance, docs/guarantees.md, docs/integrations.md, docs/status.md, docs/testing.md, docs/references.md and docs/validation.md. Build the HTTP example and execute scripts/smoke_http.py in default, --signal SIGINT and --deadline modes. Finish backend verification with scripts/jig check test and applicable work gates. Record exact commands/platform/toolchain and limits; the investigation itself did not implement or validate the proposed API, streaming behavior or macOS behavior.

Probe/fallback accessibility and response semantics remain intact during startup/drain.
- Timeout and forced cancellation preserve configured renderer status, headers and trusted correlation; observation records the actual response status without rewriting responses or adding execution policy to probes.
- Dropping a polled pending future produces one dropped HTTP event under the original subscriber with no fabricated status, no cross-registry panic and no leakage to the ambient subscriber. title: Parse provider retry delays without shortening their lower bound
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Wire delay formats need explicit clock and overflow handling before entering the core monotonic retry budget.

## Scope

Add a small outbound-provider example with an example-owned Retry-After parser and concrete parse errors; HTTP parsing and date-parser dependencies remain outside the foundation's public/normal dependency API. Declare the new target explicitly in `crates/batter/Cargo.toml` because `autoexamples = false`; enable its tests with `test = true` and document `cargo test -p batter --example provider_retry_after --locked` plus `cargo run -p batter --example provider_retry_after --locked`. Verify the applicable primary Retry-After/HTTP-date protocol sections and selected date-parser version before implementing, and record them in docs/references.md. The parser accepts one header-field value: nonnegative ASCII decimal seconds or the HTTP-date forms required by that protocol. Use injected SystemTime for date conversion and return a nonnegative Duration; a past/current date or zero seconds is a valid zero floor. Malformed or unrepresentable input is a concrete parse failure; the example stops rather than silently turning an unreadable provider instruction into an immediate retry. Convert the valid floor once at the response/classification boundary; subsequent scheduling uses the unchanged monotonic OperationContext. Missing headers add no provider floor. Parsing never decides replay safety or failure eligibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Deterministic parser tests cover zero/positive/leading-zero seconds, required date forms, injected clock before/equal/after the date, allowed surrounding header whitespace, malformed dates, signed/fractional seconds, multiple-field/list input outside the single-value contract, and numeric/date overflow. Do not read the system clock inside parser tests or re-read it during retry sleep.
- Keep valid large delays distinct from unrepresentable values: a representable provider floor beyond remaining execution time reaches RetryDecision::RetryAfter and returns StopReason::InsufficientBudget with the last application E while the total context is still live; malformed/overflow input produces the example's concrete parse failure and stops without inventing a short floor.

title: Reject non-finite Unix process watchdog bounds
description:
## Observed behavior

`scripts/scheduling_process.py::run_process` accepts non-finite `timeout` and
`reap_allowance` values. Its validation checks only `<= 0`, so both positive
infinity and NaN reach deadline arithmetic in `_run_owned_process`,
`Capture.observe_until`, and `_settle`.

On 2026-09-09 on Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 with Python 3.14.7, this repository-root
control returned successful `ProcessOutcome` values instead of raising
`ValueError` for all four cases:

```python
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=float("inf"), reap_allowance=1, output_limit=1024)
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=float("nan"), reap_allowance=1, output_limit=1024)
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=1, reap_allowance=float("inf"), output_limit=1024)
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=1, reap_allowance=float("nan"), output_limit=1024)
```

The focused `test_scheduling_process.py` suite passed all 24 tests, confirming
that the current test inventory does not reject these values. The sibling
`parallel_process.run_parallel` already requires finite positive bounds and has
an infinity/NaN regression.

## Expected behavior

The bounded Unix process owner should reject every non-finite or non-positive
duration before launching a child. A malformed bound must not be able to turn a
watchdog or termination/reap allowance into an unbounded wait.

## Affected code and likely impact

- `scripts/scheduling_process.py::run_process` validates `timeout` and
  `reap_allowance` incompletely.
- `_run_owned_process` uses `started + timeout`; `Capture.observe_until` cannot
  reach its `remaining <= 0` exit with infinity or NaN.
- `_settle` similarly derives its cleanup deadline from `reap_allowance`.

This is lower-impact because callers are repository-owned test tools with
normally constant values. If a future CLI/configured caller supplies a
non-finite value, however, a hung child can hang local or CI verification
instead of producing bounded failure evidence.

## Verification limitation

The control used `/usr/bin/true` to prove invalid values are accepted without
deliberately launching a permanently hanging child. It therefore did not wait
through the unbounded failure mode. No Linux, hosted CI, or other Python version
was exercised for this finding.
acceptance_criteria: run_process rejects NaN, infinity, zero, and negative timeout/reap allowances before spawning; focused regressions cover both fields and preserve existing bounded success, timeout, interruption, overflow, and reap behavior.

description:
## Outcome and rationale

A local retry-token budget can bound amplification but cannot decide external outcome certainty, user quota consumption or durable ownership.

## Scope and ownership

Add an optional caller-owned, finite process-local retry-token budget shared by clones; no automatic replenishment, wait queue, global budget, or durable scheduler. One token authorizes one extra factory invocation after the initial call. The initial factory remains governed by the existing total context and max_attempts and consumes no retry token. Select these consumption semantics: after ReplaySafety, expected-error classification, max_attempts, provider-floor/backoff, and cancellation/deadline preflight have permitted a replay, atomically consume one token immediately before invoking that replay's factory, with no await between successful debit and invocation. Do not reserve tokens during backoff. Cancellation or deadline expiry observed by the final preflight prevents debit and factory invocation. If that preflight permits the attempt, cancellation or expiry racing afterward may still allow atomic debit and immediate counted factory invocation; no await or second cancellation gate separates successful debit from invocation. Dropping execution before this boundary consumes no token. Once invoked, the token is permanently spent, including success, returned error, timeout, cancellation, or panic. Thus there is no speculative refund and no external-effect certainty claim. Exhaustion is a distinct typed terminal outcome retaining the last concrete error and started-attempt count. Extend the opt-in execution/result boundary delivered by batter-4c4, preserving legacy signatures/error meanings and sharing its single private execution loop rather than implementing a second scheduler. Show an interactive replay-authorized profile and a durable-attempt profile with local replay disabled and the upstream runtime retaining retry ownership; do not make this optional policy a reference-protocol dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With initial capacity N shared across concurrent executions, total extra factories invoked is at most N; initial factories are uncharged, so the budget does not claim to bound new user operations. Clones share one balance, zero capacity still permits an otherwise eligible initial call, and token exhaustion never invokes the next factory or increments its attempt count.
- Barrier-driven concurrency tests contend for the final token and prove exactly one extra factory can debit it. Count actual factory invocations and retained remaining capacity; do not test only an internal counter helper.
- Cancellation, deadline expiry, or dropping the execution while waiting in backoff consumes no token. Once an extra factory is invoked, cancellation, timeout, returned error, success, or unwinding panic does not refund it. Tests observe the actual before/after boundary; no delay-based guess stands in for it.
- ReplaySafety::Never, classifier Stop, max_attempts exhaustion, and a provider floor leaving insufficient total time consume no retry token. Cancellation or total expiry observed by final preflight is interruption without debit. A race after that preflight may consume a token only together with its counted invocation; no-await does not make clock/cancellation/decrement one atomic operation. Token exhaustion is distinguishable from AttemptsExhausted/InsufficientBudget and retains the last E and actual count; it is not fabricated as cancellation or a returned application error.

- Examples/tests distinguish local amplification tokens from user quota and durable attempt reservations. The durable profile permits one local factory per upstream attempt; the interactive profile requires caller replay authorization. Provider/effect/durable lifetime counts remain owned by the reference protocol tasks.
- A single opt-in execution combines per-attempt caps, shared tokens, jitter and provider floors. A started extra attempt that times out spends its token; interruption/backoff before invocation spends none. Distinct typed attempt/total/token outcomes retain prior E and actual counts, and all existing entrypoints keep their meaning.
